//: AgenTeX headless CI permission settings — passed to claude via --settings (ci_gate.js uses this file by default; copy it into your project to extend). Under --permission-mode dontAsk anything NOT allowed below is DENIED (deny-by-default): a denied tool ends the session without a verdict and the gate fails closed to exit 2 — never a wrong PASS/FAIL. Derived from settings.example.json (the interactive recommendation).
//notes: allow > Bash(node:*) covers the plugin's bundled scripts (preflight.js, spec_drivers.js, init_run.js, merge_run.js, run_api.js, run_db.js, ask_kb.js, session.js, fetch_baseline.js, make_html_report.js, write_verdict.js). To narrow it, replace with 'Bash(node <installed plugin path>/skills:*)'.

deny > .env and key material: the bundled scripts read secrets from the environment themselves; the session never needs to READ them, so those reads are denied rather than trusted. test/.auth/** is secret-grade saved-login state — never readable here and NEVER a published pipeline artifact.

deny > the interactive recommendation's 'ask' entries (bare curl/sqlcmd, close-all/kill-all, destructive az) are denied outright here: under dontAsk there is nobody to ask. API/DB steps run through the cataloged node runners, which stay allowed.

read scope > Read(./**) covers the CONSUMER project only. The plugin's own files (references, bundled scripts, templates) become readable via the `--add-dir <plugin-root>` argument ci_gate.js passes at spawn time from its self-resolved install location — a read-oriented grant this static file cannot carry; do not widen Read() here to compensate.

deny > Edit(./src/**) protects the application source only if it lives in ./src — repoint at your real source folder; a test run never needs to write there (it writes under test/ and executions/). Edit(path) rules cover every file-editing tool (Write, NotebookEdit included); path rules on those tools are never consulted and warn at startup, so none are listed.

shell rules > every Bash(...) rule has a PowerShell(...) twin: which set applies is decided by the runner's shell tool (Bash on Linux/macOS, PowerShell on Windows), so the unmatched set is inert and one template serves Linux and Windows runners. The PowerShell deny set also names the PowerShell spellings of the denied verbs (Remove-Item and its rm/del/rd/rmdir aliases, Invoke-WebRequest/iwr and Invoke-RestMethod/irm for curl). When you edit a shell rule, edit its twin too.
